answer: Randomized admission lottery uses a beacon cipher to seal each applicant's slot seed before the round opens. An agent must land its seed inside a narrow winner band, so mass identities yield only scattergun odds and each attempt spends real work. A failed draw leaves a ripple of wasted compute and registration latency, while a winning ticket still needs a live meadow of distinct peers to route through. Attacker's cost scales linearly with identities, so precomputing seeds buys nothing.
